First, note that the index $n$ starts from $2.$ However, it is still a geometric series because it is in the form $\sum a{r}^{n}.$ 

In this case, the first term is ${a}_{2},$ and so the sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of this geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{2}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

For the first few terms, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2} & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{2}=\frac{16}{25} \\ {a}_{3} & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{3}=\frac{64}{125}\end{aligned}
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{3}}{{a}_{2}}=\frac{(\frac{64}{125})}{(\frac{16}{25})}=\frac{4}{5}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=2}^{\infty }{(\frac{4}{5})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{2}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{16}{25})}{(1-\frac{4}{5})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{16}{25})}{(\frac{1}{5})} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}\cdot 5 \\  & =\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
